l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: This is the first volume of Kojiki, the age of the gods, presented by Yasumaro as a record compiled from traditions memorized by Hiyeda no Are under the Empress’s command. It begins with the birth of the separate Heavenly Deities and the command to Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites to create the drifting land. Their first failed union is corrected, producing the Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands and further islands, followed by many deities. Female-Who-Invites dies after bearing the Fire Deity; Male-Who-Invites kills that child, seeks her in Hades, escapes its pollution, and purifies himself. From this purification come the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Moon-Night Possessor, and Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness is expelled after violent offenses against Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, whose withdrawal into the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling darkens the world until the deities lure her out. He later kills Princess-of-Great-Food, defeats the eight-forked serpent, discovers the Herb-Quelling Great Sword, and settles at Suga. The narrative then follows Master-of-the-Great-Land, also Great-Name-Possessor, through persecution, aid from the White Hare of Inaba, trials in the Nether-Distant-Land, marriages, descendants, and the making and consolidation of the land. Heaven eventually seeks control of the Central Land of Reed-Plains: failed envoys delay the mission, but Master-of-the-Great-Land yields it after his sons comply, in return for a great abode and respectful service. Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty descends from Heaven to rule, aided by Prince of Saruta and divine regalia. His line continues through Princess-Blossoming-Brilliantly-Like-the-Flowers-of-the-Trees, whose fiery childbirth produces Fire-Shine and Fire-Subside. Fire-Subside gains help from the Ocean-Possessor, subdues his elder brother with tide jewels, and fathers Heaven’s-Sun-Height-Prince-Wave-limit-Brave-Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely, ending the volume’s stated span.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A record compiled from emperors’ genealogies and ancient family-preserved words, translated by Basil Hall Chamberlain. Its three volumes unfold from Heaven and Earth’s separation through the august reign at Woharida.

l: Yasumaro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Court Noble Yasumaro, following the Imperial Decree, records ancient words learned by heart by Hiyeda no Are, compiles Kojiki in three volumes, explains its writing, and presents it to the Empress.

l: eight hundred myriad Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The eight hundred myriad Deities are a divine assembly. Amid ominous voices and portents, they gather, consult, and help devise the plan that brings the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity out. They punish and expel High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, then assemble at the Tranquil River of Heaven with Deity Thought-Includer and agree to send Deity Ame-no-ho-hi to subdue the violent and savage Earthly Deities.

l: the Empire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Empire is a polity pacified through imperial accession, governed by Heavenly Sovereigns from the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka, and described as purified and enlarged so its country’s basis and monarchy’s foundation endure for later ages.

l: Heavenly Sovereign who governed the Eight Great Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heavenly Sovereign governed the Eight Great Islands from the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka, ascended to the Heavenly seat, established divine reason and good customs, and ordered imperial chronicles and ancient words corrected and recorded.

l: Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_the_seat_of Heavenly Sovereign who governed the Eight Great Islands [during his reign] The Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka was the place from which the Heavenly Sovereign governed the Eight Great Islands. It was also the place where he ascended to the Heavenly seat.

l: chronicles of the emperors, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Chronicles of the emperors, said to contain falsehoods, are ordered by the Heavenly Sovereign to be selected, examined, corrected, and recorded for later ages.

l: original words in the possession of the various families, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: deviate_from exact truth [according to the Heavenly Sovereign] The original words in the possession of the various families were reported to differ from exact truth and to be enlarged by falsehoods. They were to be examined, with falsehoods erased and the truth determined.

l: Hiyeda no Are, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Hiyeda no Are is an exceptionally intelligent twenty-eight-year-old retainer, able to repeat what he sees and retain what he hears. By command of the Heavenly Sovereign, he memorizes imperial genealogies and former ages’ family-held words, later recorded by Yasumaro.

l: Empress, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Empress, versed in Triad and residing at Purple Palace, obtains Unity and governs the Empire, illuminating and nourishing its people; regretting errors in older records, she commands Yasumaro to record Hiyeda no Are’s memorized words.

l: Wa-do, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Wa-do is an era marked by the Empress’s fourth-year command to Yasumaro to record old words and the fifth-year presentation of the completed work.

l: Imperial Decree, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: An Imperial Decree orders chronicles of emperors and ancient words selected, examined, and recorded by Yasumaro from Hiyeda no Are’s memorized words, to correct falsehoods, preserve truth, and transmit it to later ages.

l: First Volume, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: First Volume begins with Heaven and Earth’s separation, then recounts the origins of Deities, islands, and men, the descent of Ho-no-ni-ni-gi, and the Island of the Dragon-Fly’s traversal, ending with Prince-Wave-Limit-Brave-Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely.

l: Heaven and Earth separation, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The separation of Heaven and Earth marks the beginning of the recorded account. It is associated with the commencement of creation and the emergence of the Three Deities.

l: imperial accession, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The imperial accession described in the preface occurs when the Heavenly Sovereign ascends to the Heavenly seat at the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka. He then obtains heavenly supremacy and annexes the Eight Wildernesses.

l: compilation of the records, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The compilation corrects deviations and falsehoods in imperial chronicles and ancient words: commanded by Empress, based on memorized old words, Yasumaro selects, arranges, explains, and records Three Volumes.

l: Court Noble Futo no Yasumaro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Court Noble Futo no Yasumaro, also known as Yasumaro, was an Officer of the Upper Division of the Fifth Rank and Fifth Order of Merit who reverently presented the completed Three Volumes on the 28th day of the first moon of Wa-dō’s fifth year.

l: The Beginning of Heaven and Earth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a beginning It marks the time when the first Deities were born.

l: Plain of High Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A heavenly, high plain where three deities are born; it darkens when Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires, shakes during Heavenly-Alarming Female’s performance, and becomes light when the deity returns.

l: Master-of-the-August-Centre-of-Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity born alone in the Plain of High Heaven when Heaven and Earth began, then hid its person.

l: High-August-Producing-Wondrous Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity born alone in the Plain of High Heaven when Heaven and Earth began, then hid their person.

l: Divine-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A Deity born alone in the Plain of High Heaven when Heaven and Earth began, then hid its person.

l: Pleasant-Reed-Shoot-Prince-Elder Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A Deity born alone from a reed-shoot-like sprout while young Earth drifted medusa-like, then hid its person.

l: Heavenly-Eternally-Standing-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A Deity born alone from a reed-shoot-like thing as young Earth drifted medusa-like, then hid its person.

l: the five Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a separate Heavenly Deities They comprise Master-of-the-August-Centre-of-Heaven, High-August-Producing-Wondrous Deity, Divine-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Pleasant-Reed-Shoot-Prince-Elder Deity, and Heavenly-Eternally-Standing-Deity. They are separate Heavenly Deities.

l: Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heaven began with Earth when three deities were born. It has the Floating Bridge of Heaven and an eight-forking road linked to passage with the Central Land of Reed-Plains. His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness ascends there, and princes are commanded to descend from it.

l: Earth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Earth, once young and floating-oil-like, drifted medusa-like as two Deities were born.

l: Seven Divine Generations, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a divine generations The Seven Divine Generations comprise the Earthly-Eternally-Standing-Deity, the Luxuriant-Integrating-Master-Deity, and five pairs of deities ending with the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites. The two solitary Deities each constitute one generation, while each succeeding pair constitutes a generation.

l: Heavenly Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heavenly Deities command Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites, use divination, send them to amend words, and give them a heavenly jewelled spear to make drifting land.

l: Earthly-Eternally-Standing-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A solitary Deity, first of the succeeding Seven Divine Generations, is born alone and hides person.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites is an august male Deity, one of the Seven Divine Generations and elder brother of the Female-Who-Invites. With her, he is commanded to make, consolidate, and give birth to the drifting land; he stirs brine with the heavenly jewelled spear, makes lands, and jointly gives birth to fourteen islands and thirty-five Deities. After ritual words, he admires her, but later laments exchanging the Princess-Who-Invites for their child; his tears produce the Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity, and he cuts off the head of the Deity Shining-Elder with his ten-grasp sabre. He follows the Female-Who-Invites to the Land of Hades seeking her return so their lands may be finished, then flees her rotting body, delays pursuers with his head-dress and comb, repels them with peaches, and seals the pass with a rock. Polluted by Hades, he purifies himself at a river-mouth, producing Deities. Finally he begets three illustrious children, assigns domains, expels His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, and dwells at Taga.

l: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites is a deity, the younger sister of His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites and one of the Seven Divine Generations. With him, she is commanded to make, consolidate, and give birth to the drifting land, stirring brine with the heavenly jewelled spear. She gives birth to Deity-of-Fire and other deities; the fire birth burns her private parts, causing sickness, divine retirement, and burial at Mount Hiba. In Hades, she has eaten of its furnace and considers returning, but after her brother looks at her, she sends pursuers and pursues him herself. Threatening to strangle a thousand people daily, she becomes the Great-Deity-of-Hades and is also called Road-Reaching-Great-Deity.

l: drifting land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a land [subject of the command given to Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites] The drifting land is the land that the Heavenly Deities command the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites to make, consolidate, and give birth to.

l: heavenly jewelled spear, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a spear [heavenly and jewelled] The Heavenly Deities grant the heavenly jewelled spear to the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites. They use it to stir the brine, and the brine dripping from its end becomes an island.

l: Island of Onogoro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Island formed as brine drips from the heavenly jewelled spear, piles up after stirring curdle-curdle, and is not jointly born by the two Deities.

l: command to make, consolidate, and give birth to the drifting land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A command from the Heavenly Deities directs the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites to stir brine and produce Onogoro.

l: Courtship of the Deities the Male-Who-Invites and the Female Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a courtship The Courtship concerns Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat after they descend from Heaven onto the island. They erect an heavenly august pillar and an hall of eight fathoms, agree to unite for procreation, and produce Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A male deity descended from Heaven on an island, with a younger sister and heavenly structures. He proposes procreation, directs their ritual circling, reproves her speech, and helps produce Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A female deity descended from Heaven, on an island with a heavenly august pillar and hall of eight fathoms. After circling the pillar, she speaks, unites with her elder brother Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat, and gives birth to Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: island, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The island is where Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat descend from Heaven. On it, they erect an heavenly august pillar and an hall of eight fathoms.

l: Hirudinem, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: First child of Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat, placed in a boat of reeds and set afloat.

l: Island of Aha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Island of Aha is produced after Hirudinem by Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat, but not reckoned among their children.

l: the two Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The two Deities judge their first children unsuccessful, consult the Heavenly Deities, descend and amend their words, and repeat their ritual with the Male-Who-Invites speaking first. They then give birth to the Island of Ahaji, eight islands, and six additional islands, including Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly.

l: the birth of the Eight Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: After the Male-Who-Invites speaks first, the two Deities give birth to eight islands. These islands give rise to the name Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands because they were born first.

l: the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, after repeating their ritual.

l: the Island of Futa-no, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Island of Futa-no, born in Iyo to the two Deities, has one body and four faces: Iyo, Sanuki, Aha, and Tosa.

l: the Islands of Mitsu-go, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Islands of Mitsu-go, also called Heavenly-Great-Heart-Youth, are born near Oki with one body and four separately named faces: Tsukushi, Toyo, Hi, and Kumaso.

l: the Island of Iki, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: has_other_name Heaven's One-Pillar The two Deities give birth to the Island of Iki, also called Heaven's One-Pillar.

l: the Island of Tsu, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: has_other_name Heavenly-Hand-net-Good-Princess The two Deities give birth to the Island of Tsu, also called Heavenly-Hand-net-Good-Princess.

l: the Island of Sado, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Sado.

l: Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: has_other_name Heavenly-August-Sky-Luxuriant-Dragon-fly-Lord-Youth The two Deities give birth to Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly, also called Heavenly-August-Sky-Luxuriant-Dragon-fly-Lord-Youth. It is the eighth island born among the Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands.

l: Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_named_after the eight islands [born first] The name Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands originates from the eight islands that were born first: the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, the Island of Futa-no, the Islands of Mitsu-go, the Island of Iki, the Island of Tsu, the Island of Sado, and Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly.

l: Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing is the first deity born in the renewed sequence of births after the countries. He is included among the ten deities born from Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing to Princess-of-Autumn.

l: Great-Ocean-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Ocean-Possessor receives Fire-Subside, gives him Luxuriant-Jewel-Princess in marriage, finds the lost fish-hook through fishes, explains its return, and gives tide-flowing and tide-ebbing jewels.

l: Prince-of-Swift-Autumn, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Prince-of-Swift-Autumn, Deity of the Water-Gates, is born after Great-House-Prince and other deities. With his younger sister Princess-of-Swift-Autumn, he holds separate dominion of river and gives birth to eight water-related deities.

l: Princess-of-Swift-Autumn, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity and younger sister of Prince-of-Swift-Autumn, born Deity of the Water-Gates, gives birth with him to eight water-related deities.

l: Princess-of-Great-Food, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Princess-of-Great-Food is a deity who makes dishes from dainty things and offers them to High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. She takes them from her body, is killed by him, and silkworms, rice-seeds, millet, beans, and barley are born from her body.

l: birth of the various deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a section After the birth of countries, the deities begin giving birth to various deities. The births include deities associated with water, wind, trees, mountains, moors, passes, valleys, food, and fire.

l: Deity-of-Fire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Deity-of-Fire was born to Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites. Through giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire, she was burned and ultimately divinely retired.

l: Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A Deity born from His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites' tears, who dwells at Konomoto near Unewo on Mount Kagu.

l: Mount Hiba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Mount Hiba is a place at the boundary of the Land of Idzumo and Land of Hahaki, where Male-Who-Invites buried Female-Who-Invites.

l: Land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Land of Idzumo is a land containing Ifuya-Pass, Miho, the little shore of Inasa, and the shore of Tagishi. His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness sought a palace there, while Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land dwelt at Miho and had an heavenly august abode at Tagishi. It is the place from which the Deity departs to the Land of Yamato.

l: birth of the Deity-of-Fire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: causes divine retirement of the Princess-Who-Invites [after her private parts are burnt] The birth of the Deity-of-Fire burned the august private parts of Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites. After this birth, she sickened, lay down, and divinely retired.

l: divine retirement of the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_followed_by burial of the Female-Who-Invites [on Mount Hiba] The Princess-Who-Invites divinely retired after giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire and becoming sick. Her divinely retired body was buried on Mount Hiba by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites.

l: burial of the Female-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites buried the divinely retired Deity the Female-Who-Invites on Mount Hiba. The burial place was at the boundary of the Land of Idzumo and the Land of Hahaki.

l: The Slaying of the Fire-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a section The unit concerns the slaying of the Deity Shining-Elder by His Augustness the Male-Who-invites and the Deities born from the sword and from the slain body.

l: the Deity Shining-Elder, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Shining-Elder, child of His Augustness the Male-Who-invites, is beheaded by him; eight Deities are born from his body.

l: Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity, also called the Brave-Snapping-Deity and Luxuriant-Snapping Deity, is sent with Deity Heavenly-Bird-Boat to obtain the Central Land of Reed-Plains, defeats Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm, gains its yield, and reports its pacification to Heaven.

l: Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a sword name [name of the sword] Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended is one name of the sword with which His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off the head of the Deity Shining-Elder.

l: Majestic Point-Blade-Extended, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a sword name [another name of the sword] Majestic Point-Blade-Extended is another name for the sword with which His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off the head of the Deity Shining-Elder.

l: ten-grasp sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A ten-grasp sword girded on His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, whose blood from point, upper part, and hilt gives birth to eight Deities.

l: Land of Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Land of Hades, also called Ifuya-Pass, is the residence of Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites after she eats from its furnace, containing a palace, deities, pursuers, and warriors.

l: lands made by the siblings, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: are_not_finished_making unfinished [at the time of the brother's return request] The lands made by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites and Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites are not yet finished making.

l: Even Pass of Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A pass of Hades where His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites repels pursuers with three peaches and blocks the passage with a thousand-draught rock; the Great Deity pursues Great-Name-Possessor and calls commands from afar. Later called Ifuya-Pass in the Land of Idzumo.

l: three peaches, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Three peaches at the Even Pass of Hades help His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites smite pursuers and are designated Their Augustnesses Great-Divine-Fruit.

l: thousand-draught rock, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A thousand-draught rock, drawn by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, blocks the Even Pass of Hades between him and Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites during leave-takings.

l: Great-Deity-of-Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_another_name_for Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites is called the Great-Deity-of-Hades after she pursues and reaches His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites.

l: Ifuya-Pass, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_in Land of Idzumo The Ifuya-Pass is the later name for the Even Pass of Hades in the Land of Idzumo.

l: Central Land of Reed-Plains, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Central Land of Reed-Plains is a land containing its people and lasting a Thousand Autumns, of Long-Five-Hundred-Autumns. It becomes dark when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires and light when she comes forth. Charged to an august child of the Heavenly Deities, it is noisy and filled with violent, savage Earthly Deities. Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land yields it up; the Heavenly-Young-Prince is sent to pacify it, it is pacified by the Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity, and Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty is sent to dwell and rule there.

l: The Purification of the August Person, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a section It concerns the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites cleansing himself after coming to a hideous and polluted land. The purification includes removing the things on his person and bathing in different parts of the water.

l: a small river-mouth near Tachibana in Himuka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A small river-mouth in Himuka near Tachibana, where the Male-Who-Invites purifies and cleanses himself on an ahagi-covered plain.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Bottom, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity [possessor of the ocean bottom] He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the bottom of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Bottom, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity, one of three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi, born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes underwater.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Middle, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity [possessor of the ocean middle] He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes in the middle of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Middle, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity, one of three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi, is born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes in middle water.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Surface, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity [possessor of the ocean surface] He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the top of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Surface, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity and one of three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi, born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes atop water.

l: the three Ocean-Possessing Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Three Deities possess the ocean’s bottom, middle, and surface, and the Chiefs of Adzumi revere them as ancestral deities.

l: the Chiefs of Adzumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Chiefs of Adzumi revere three Ocean-Possessing Deities as ancestral Deities and descend from His Augustness Utsushi-hi-gana-saku.

l: the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deities [three in number] They are His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Bottom, His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Middle, and His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Surface.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity is a deity born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his left august eye. Receiving the August necklace, she is charged to rule the Plain-of-High-Heaven. When her younger sibling, His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, approaches, she arms herself with jewels, bow, and arrows; they swear and produce children, and she claims the five male Deities born last. After his ravages culminate in the release of a flayed heavenly piebald horse in the weaving-hall, she withdraws into the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, bringing darkness and eternal night. She emerges after seeing the mirror, restoring light to the Plain of High Heaven and the Central Land of Reed-Plains. Thereafter she exercises heavenly authority: she governs alongside other deities, convenes the eight hundred myriad Deities, sends envoys concerning the yielding of the Central Land of Reed-Plains, and commands His Augustness Heaven's-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty to descend and rule it.

l: His Augustness, Moon-Night Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity He is born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his right august eye.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness is a Deity, born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his august nose. Charged to rule the Sea-Plain, he refuses it, weeps to depart for his deceased mother's Nether Distant Land, and is divinely expelled. After ascending to Heaven to take leave of his elder sister Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, he swears with her and produces deities, becoming parent of the three female Deities born first. Claiming victory, he commits increasingly violent evil acts against her ricefields, palace, and weaving-hall. The eight hundred myriad Deities fine, mutilate, and expel him. He then kills Princess-of-Great-Food after judging her offering filth. Descending to the River Hi, he protects Wondrous-Inada-Princess by intoxicating and slaying the eight-forked serpent of Koshi, and discovers the great sword.

l: the purification of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A purification of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites at a small river-mouth near Tachibana in Himuka, after reaching a polluted land, produces Deities by removing garments and bathing.

l: the bathing of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: gives_rise_to the fourteen Deities born from bathing his august person He first plunges into the middle reach because the upper reach is too rapid and the lower reach too sluggish. As he bathes at the bottom, middle, and surface of the water and washes his eyes and nose, multiple Deities are born.

l: Investiture of the Three Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites invests the three illustrious children with authority over different domains.

l: the Three Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a illustrious august children [be begotten by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites] The Three Deities are the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Moon-Night-Possessor, and His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. The first two assume their assigned rule, while the third does not.

l: Moon-Night-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_charged_to_rule the dominion [of the Night] Moon-Night-Possessor is charged to rule the Dominion of the Night.

l: Plain-of-High-Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Plain-of-High-Heaven is assigned to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity to rule.

l: Sea-Plain, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Sea-Plain is assigned to His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness to rule, but he does not take up the charge.

l: Crying and Weeping of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Crying and Weeping of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness is a Great Deity whose intense weeping withers mountains, dries waters, and brings omens of woe. He searches Idzumo, builds and dwells in the palace of Suga, makes an august song, and appoints and names its headman. He dwells in Nether-Distant-Land, receives and tests Deity Great-Name-Possessor, then commands him to rule the land.

l: Nether Distant Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a deceased mother's land [of His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness] The Nether Distant Land is the deceased mother's land to which His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness wishes to depart.

l: The August Expulsion of His-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A divine expulsion removes His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness after his departure wish is rejected and Deities fine, mutilate, and banish him.

l: The August Oath, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a oath The August Oath is established when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness swear to each other and produce children from a sabre and curved jewels.

l: swearing and producing children, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A test of sincerity at Tranquil River of Heaven unfolds as two deities swear, produce children, and create deities from mist.

l: ten-grasp sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A ten-grasp sabre girded on His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness is drawn and used to cut the eight-forked serpent into pieces.

l: Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity, first of three female deities born from Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity’s breath, also called Princess-of-the-Island-of-the-Offing, dwelling in Munakata’s Inner temple.

l: Her Augustness Lovely-Island-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity also called Her Augustness Good-Princess, second of three female Deities born from Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity's breath, dwells at Munakata's middle temple.

l: Her Augustness Princess-of-the-Torrent, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity born from Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity's breath, third of three female Deities, dwells in Munakata's outer temple.

l: His Augustness Truly-Conquer-I-Conqueror-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity and Heir Apparent, he fathers Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty and reports the child should descend in his place.

l: His Augustness Prince-Lord-of-Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity born from His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness's breath, His Augustness Prince-Lord-of-Heaven is chiefly identified as ancestor of numerous rulers, chiefs, suzerains, departmental suzerains, and territorial lords across several lands.

l: five deities born from the mist, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A group of five male deities, born last from Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity’s things, are declared her children.

l: The August Declaration of the Division of the August Male Children and the August Female Children, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a declaration This declaration assigns the five male Deities born last to Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and the three female Deities born first to His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. It also states where the three female Deities dwell and identifies their reverence by the Dukes of Munakata.

l: The August Ravages of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a ravages This section concerns the ravages committed by His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness against Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. He breaks down ricefield divisions, fills up ditches, strews excrements in the palace, and releases a flayed heavenly piebald horse into the weaving-hall.

l: the three female Deities born first, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a female Deities [born first] The three female Deities born first are declared to be the children of His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness because their birth was from a thing of his. They dwell in the three temples of Munakata.

l: the three Great Deities held in reverence by the Dukes of Munakata, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Great Deities [three in number] The three Great Deities held in reverence by the Dukes of Munakata are Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess, Her Augustness Lovely-Island-Princess, and Her Augustness Princess-of-the-Torrent.

l: His Augustness Brave-Rustic-Illuminator, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His Augustness Brave-Rustic-Illuminator is a child of His Augustness Ame-no-hohi, one of five children born afterwards. He is identified as ancestor of rulers in Idzumo, Musashi, Upper and Lower Unakami, Izhimu, and Tohotsu-Afumi, and of the departmental suzerains of Tsu.

l: Munakata, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Munakata is a place with Inner, middle, and outer temples, where three female Deities dwell and three Great Deities are revered by the Dukes of Munakata.

l: Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a rock dwelling [heavenly] The Heavenly Rock-Dwelling is the place into which the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires. Its door is closed and fastened, then later opened slightly so that she can gaze upon the mirror and come forth.

l: door (Heavenly Rock-Dwelling), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, fastened by the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, is opened slightly after the Heavenly-Alarming Female performs.

l: eternal night, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a night [eternal] Eternal night prevails after the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity closes herself inside the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling. The long-singing birds of eternal night are assembled and made to sing as part of the plan to bring her out.

l: Deity Thought-Includer, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Thought-Includer is a Deity, child of the High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, who helps govern the Heavenly Deities. Ordered to devise a plan at the divine assembly, he addresses subduing Earthly Deities, joins the decision to send Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, recommends Heavenly-Young-Prince and Name-Crying-Female, and is worshipped at temple of Isuzu.

l: High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity, also called High-Integrating-Deity, asks which Deity should investigate the Heavenly-Young-Prince’s failure to report.

l: mirror, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A mirror eight feet long is tied to a true cleyera japonica; Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord and Great-Jewel present it, drawing forth Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: His Augustness Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A heavenly ancestor lord and one of five company chiefs, ancestor of the Nakatomi Chieftains, assists a plan through divination and liturgies, then helps reveal the mirror and draw out the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: Great-Jewel, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Great-Jewel, an Augustness, receives offerings and divers things, assists the plan, pushes forward a mirror, and draws a bottom-tied rope along her back.

l: Heavenly Mount Kagu, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heavenly Mount Kagu is a mount providing a true stag shoulder-blade, cherrybark, five-hundred-branched true cleyera japonica, heavenly clubmoss, heavenly spindle-tree, and bamboo-grass for plans and performance.

l: Heavenly Hand-Strength-Male-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Hidden beside Heavenly Rock-Dwelling’s door, he takes Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity’s hand and draws her out when she emerges.

l: Heavenly-Alarming-Female, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heavenly-Alarming-Female is a female Deity, a delicate yet deity-conquering Her Augustness, one of five chiefs of companies and ancestress of the Duchesses of Saru. Wearing heavenly clubmoss as a sash, a heavenly spindle-tree head-dress, and bamboo-grass as a posy, she performs before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling as if possessed. The performance shakes the Plain of High Heaven and makes the eight hundred myriad Deities laugh, causing Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity to open the door slightly; she claims greater illustriousness. She questions a radiant Deity, descends among the five chiefs, escorts Deity Prince of Saruta back, bears his august name, gathers fishes for the august son of the Heavenly Deities, and cuts the silent bèche-de-mer’s mouth.

l: Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Ancestor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: causes_to_be_used_as seeds [the things born in Princess-of-Great-Food's body] Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Ancestor causes the things born from the body of Princess-of-Great-Food to be taken and used as seeds.

l: seeds, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Seeds are taken from Princess-of-Great-Food’s body: silkworms from her head, rice-seeds from her eyes, millet from her ears, small beans from her nose, barley from her private parts, and large beans from her fundament.

l: River Hi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: River Hi in Land of Idzumo begins at grieving head-waters and ends flowing changed into blood after the serpent is cut apart.

l: old man (Foot-Stroking-Elder), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Earthly Deity, child of Great-Mountain-Possessor and headman of Suga, loses seven daughters to the eight-forked serpent, offers Wondrous-Inada-Princess, then is appointed palace headman and renamed.

l: old woman (Hand-Stroking Elder), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Earthly Deity, wife and mother, weeps with Foot-Stroking-Elder and Wondrous-Inada-Princess over the serpent's expected arrival.

l: Wondrous-Inada-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Young daughter of Foot-Stroking-Elder and Hand-Stroking Elder, taken by His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness and transformed into a comb.

l: Land of Koshi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Land of Koshi is the distant land where the Princess of Nuna-kaha lives. The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears travels there to woo her.

l: eight-forked serpent of Koshi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: An eight-forked serpent from Koshi has one body, eight heads and tails, akakagachi-like eyes, and moss, chamaecyparis, and cryptomerias growing on it. Spanning eight valleys and hills, with a bloody, inflamed belly, it devours eight young girls yearly before drinking liquor, sleeping, and being cut into pieces.

l: eight-fold refined liquor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a liquor [eight-fold refined] It is prepared in eight vats as part of the trap for the eight-forked serpent of Koshi. The serpent drinks it and becomes intoxicated.

l: Herb-Quelling Great Sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A great sword found in the middle tail of the eight-forked serpent after the ten-grasp sabre breaks, taken and reported by His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.

l: descent from Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness descends from Heaven to Tori-kami and identifies himself as elder brother to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: annual devouring of the daughters, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: An annual habit in which the eight-forked serpent of Koshi devours eight daughters, leaving Wondrous-Inada-Princess awaiting its arrival.

l: preparation of the liquor trap, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness orders eight refined liquor vats, a fenced eight-gate setup, platforms, and vats; Foot-Stroking-Elder and Hand-Stroking Elder complete the preparations.

l: serpent's intoxication, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A state caused by drinking liquor: the eight-forked serpent drinks from vats, becomes intoxicated, then all its heads sleep.

l: slaying of the eight-forked serpent, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness draws his ten-grasp sabre and cuts the sleeping eight-forked serpent into pieces. The River Hi consequently flows as a river of blood.

l: discovery of the great sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A discovery unfolds when His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness investigates a broken sabre and finds the Herb-Quelling Great Sword within the serpent's middle tail.

l: Suga, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a place Suga was the place where His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness built a palace after saying that his august heart was pure there. The place is now called Suga, and clouds rose from it when the palace was first built.

l: palace of Suga, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A palace in Suga, built for His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness; clouds rose at its founding and Deity Foot-Stroking-Elder became Headman.

l: august song, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: says Eight clouds arise The august song was made by His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness when clouds rose from the palace of Suga. It said that eight clouds arise and that the eight-fold fence of Idzumo makes an eight-fold fence for the spouses to retire within.

l: eight-fold fence of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The eight-fold fence of Idzumo makes an eight-fold enclosure for spouses to retire within, as described in the august song.

l: The August Ancestors of the Deity-Master-of-the-Great Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a genealogical account The August Ancestors of the Deity-Master-of-the-Great Land are presented through a genealogy of marriages and births. The lineage culminates in the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land.

l: Deity Eight-Island Ruler, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Eight-Island Ruler is a deity born to unnamed parents, counted among seventeen generations, who marries several consorts and parents Great-Harvest Deity, August-Spirit-of-Food, and Deity Fuha-no-moji-Ku-nu-su-nu.

l: Deity Great-Mountain-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Great-Mountain-Possessor fathers two daughters, sends them to Heaven's-Sun-Height-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty, and declares rejection brings frailty.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land is a deity also called Deity Great-Name-Possessor, Deity-of-the-Reed-Plains, Deity of Eight-Thousand-Spears, and Deity-Spirit-of-the-Living-Land. Begotten by Deity Heavenly-Brandishing-Prince-Lord and Young-Princess-of-the-Small-Country, he begins among eighty brethren as their bag-carrying attendant; the White Hare of Inaba foretells that he will obtain Princess of Yakami. After pursuing his half-brethren, he is commanded to assume the role Master-of-the-Great-Land. He seeks spouses, woos Princess of Nuna-kaha in the Land of Koshi, pledges by the cup with Her Augustness the Forward-Princess, and weds several deities and princesses, begetting children including Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne, Her Augustness High-Princess, Deity Thing-Sign-Master, and Deity Bird-Growing-Ears. Dwelling at Miho, he seeks help to make the land and asks how Deity illuminating the sea should be laid to rest. As ruler of the Central Land of Reed-Plains, he receives Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, then is asked to yield the land. After consulting his sons, he consents in exchange for a great abode and respectful service to his children, and is established at a Heavenly august abode.

l: eighty Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Eighty Deities travel to Inaba seeking marriage with the Princess of Yakami. They harm the White Hare of Inaba and repeatedly try to kill their brother, Deity Great-Name-Possessor, who is restored and escapes. He then pursues, scatters, and drives them onto slopes and into rivers.

l: Princess of Yakami, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Princess of Yakami in Inaba rejects eighty Deities’ proposals and chooses to marry Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land.

l: White Hare of Inaba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A hare from the Island of Oki deceives sea crocodiles to cross, but the last strips off its clothing. Harmed by eighty Deities’ instructions, it is restored with fresh water and sedge pollen by Great-Name-Possessor, becoming the Hare Deity.

l: Inaba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a land Inaba is the land associated with the Princess of Yakami and the White Hare of Inaba. The eighty Deities travel there seeking the princess, and Cape Keta is where they encounter the hare.

l: Nether-Distant-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a land [nether-distant] The Nether-Distant-Land is where His Impetuous-Male-Augustness dwells. The Deity Great-Name-Possessor goes there to receive his counsel.

l: Forward-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Forward-Princess, daughter of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, marries Great-Name-Possessor, protects and helps him escape, then bears Tree-Fork-Deity and Deity-of-August-Wells.

l: Deity Great-Name-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Ugly-Male-Deity-of-the-Reed-Plain [as named by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness] The Deity Great-Name-Possessor survives the trials imposed by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness with help from the Forward-Princess and a mouse. He ties up the Great Deity, escapes with the great life-sword, life-bow-and-arrows, and heavenly speaking-lute, pursues the eighty Deities, and begins to make the land.

l: great life-sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a sword [possessed by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness] The great life-sword is taken by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor when he escapes from the Great Deity. At the Even Pass of Hades, the Great Deity tells him to use it to pursue his half-brethren.

l: life-bow-and-arrows, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a bow and arrows [possessed by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness] The life-bow-and-arrows are taken by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor when he escapes from the Great Deity. The Great Deity tells him to use them to pursue his half-brethren.

l: half-brethren, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: are_pursued_by Deity Great-Name-Possessor [with the great life-sword and life-bow-and-arrows] The half-brethren are to be pursued by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor with the great life-sword and life-bow-and-arrows until they crouch on the august slopes of the passes and are swept into the reaches of the rivers.

l: Spirit-of-the-Living-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a Deity Great-Name-Possessor [appointed by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness] Spirit-of-the-Living-Land is another role the Great Deity commands the Deity Great-Name-Possessor to assume, with the Forward-Princess as his consort.

l: Mount Uka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: has_at_its_foot temple-pillars [in the nethermost rock-bottom] Mount Uka is named as the place at whose foot the Deity Great-Name-Possessor is commanded to make stout the temple-pillars in the nethermost rock-bottom.

l: land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Land begins when Deity Great-Name-Possessor commands Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land to make it; unable alone, the Master can make it with Deity illuminating the sea if that Deity is laid to rest well.

l: land-making, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a making of the land [undertaken by Deity Great-Name-Possessor] Land-making begins after the Deity Great-Name-Possessor pursues and scatters the eighty Deities. He is commanded to make the land as Master-of-the-Great-Land and Spirit-of-the-Living-Land.

l: marriage, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_between Forward-Princess [and Deity Great-Name-Possessor] The Forward-Princess and the Deity Great-Name-Possessor exchange glances and are married. The Great Deity later commands that she become his consort.

l: escape from the Great Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a escape [by Deity Great-Name-Possessor with Forward-Princess] The Deity Great-Name-Possessor escapes from the Great Deity after tying his hair to the rafters and blocking the floor with a five hundred draught rock. He carries off the great life-sword, life-bow-and-arrows, and heavenly speaking-lute, though the lute's sound causes the Great Deity to pull down the house.

l: Princess of Nuna-kaha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A wise, beautiful maiden in Koshi answers the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears in song, joins him at night, and becomes a dotterel, then a gentle bird.

l: wooing of the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a wooing The wooing takes place at the house of the Princess of Nuna-kaha. The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears sings outside while the Princess responds from inside, and the wooing culminates in their coition on the following night.

l: coition of the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears and the Princess of Nuna-kaha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears and Princess of Nuna-kaha do not cohabit on his arrival, then cohabit augustly the following night.

l: Her Augustness the Forward-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Deity's Chief Empress, jealous toward her husband, offers an august liquor-cup, sings exclusive devotion, and pledges herself to him.

l: the Land of Yamato, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_destination_of the Deity's departure from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato The Land of Yamato is the place to which the Deity is about to go from Idzumo.

l: the Deity's departure from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a departure [from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato] The Deity's departure from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato is prompted by distress over his Chief Empress's jealousy. He sings about flocking and departing before the cup pledge takes place.

l: the Cup Pledge, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Cup Pledge is divine words: the Deity and Her Augustness the Forward-Princess pledge by the cup, hands on each other’s necks, then remain at rest.

l: august liquor-cup, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a liquor-cup [august] The august liquor-cup is taken and offered by Her Augustness the Forward-Princess to the Deity. It is used for their pledge.

l: the Deity's jealousy, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Deity's jealousy is not described; the text says that the Deity's Chief Empress, Her Augustness the Forward-Princess, is very jealous.

l: Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity, begotten by Master-of-the-Great-Land and Torrent-Mist-Princess, is called the Great August Deity of Kamo. Dear friend of Heavenly-Young-Prince, he comes to mourn, is mistaken for the dead prince, angrily destroys the mourning-house, and flies away.

l: Her Augustness Princess Under-Shining, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Princess Under-Shining, daughter of Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, marries Heavenly-Young-Prince and wails to Heaven after his death.

l: Deity Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master, son of Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, pursues birds and catches fish at Cape Miho, supports yielding the Central Land of Reed-Plains, then conveys its presentation and disappears after overturning his boat.

l: Deity Bird-Growing-Ears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Bird-Growing-Ears, begotten by Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and Deity Bird-Ears, weds Hina-teri-nakata-bichi-wo-ikochini and begets Deity Land-Great-Wealth.

l: Deity Land-Great-Wealth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Land-Great-Wealth, begotten by Deity Bird-Growing-Ears and Hina-teri-nakata-bichi-wo-ikochini, weds Deity Ashi-nadaka and begets Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler.

l: Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler, begotten by Deity Land-Great-Wealth and Deity Ashi-nadaka, weds Princess Luck-Spirit and begets Deity Awful-Master-Prince.

l: Deity Awful-Master-Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Awful-Master-Prince, child of Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler and Princess Luck-Spirit, weds Princess Hina-rashi and begets Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi.

l: Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Begotten by Deity Awful-Master-Prince and Princess Hina-rashi, weds Deity Princess-Life-Spirit-Luck-Spirit and begets Deity Mira-na-mi.

l: Deity Mira-na-mi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Mira-na-mi, born to Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi and Princess-Life-Spirit-Luck-Spirit, weds Princess Awo-numa-oshi and begets Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi.

l: Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi, born to Deity Mira-na-mi and Princess Awo-numa-oshi, weds Young-Day-Female-Deity and begets Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth.

l: Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth, born to two deities, weds Toho-tsu-ma-chi-ne and begets Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi.

l: Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a deity Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi was begotten by Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth and the Deity Toho-tsu-ma-chi-ne. The text places this Deity at the end of the line called the Deities of seventeen generations.

l: Deities of seventeen generations, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Deities of seventeen generations extend from Deity Eight-Island-Ruler through Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi.

l: the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity is a Deity, child of the Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity. Arriving by heavenly Kagami boat in geese skins, he is identified by the Crumbling Prince, makes and consolidates the land with the Great-Name-Possessor, then crosses to the Eternal Land.

l: the Crumbling Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Crumbling Prince is the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, now a scarecrow in the mountain fields, knowing everything in the Empire despite legs that do not walk.

l: the Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_parent_of the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity [divine child] The Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity was identified as the parent of the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity. He declared that the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity and the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land should become brethren and make and consolidate the land.

l: the land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The land was made and consolidated conjointly by the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity.

l: the two Deities the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Two Deities, called brethren, conjointly make and consolidate Idzumo until Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity crosses to Eternal Land.

l: making and consolidating the land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_done_by the two Deities the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity [conjointly] Making and consolidating the land was the joint work of the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, after they were instructed to become brethren.

l: Deity illuminating the sea, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity illuminating the sea is a deity who appears, offers with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land to make land if reverently laid to rest, requires reverent worship at Yamato's green fence and the eastern mountain's top, and dwells atop Mount Mimoro.

l: Yamato's green fence, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Yamato's green fence is named as the place where Deity illuminating the sea should be reverently worshipped.

l: eastern mountain's top, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The eastern mountain's top is named as the place where Deity illuminating the sea should be reverently worshipped.

l: Mount Mimoro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Mount Mimoro is identified as the mountain whose top is the dwelling place of Deity illuminating the sea.

l: making the land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Making the land is an undertaking that Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land cannot accomplish alone. Deity illuminating the sea offers to undertake making the land together with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land.

l: reverently worshipping the Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Reverently worshipping the Deity is required at Yamato's green fence, the eastern mountain's top, in order for Deity illuminating the sea to be laid to rest well.

l: Great-Harvest-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Great-Harvest-Deity is a person who weds Princess [of?] Inu, Refulgent-Princess, and Princess Ame-shiru-karu-midzu. He fathers sixteen deities, beginning with August-Spirit-of-the-Great-Land and ending with Great-Earth-Deity, including five children with Princess [of?] Inu.

l: Swift-Mountain-Dwelling, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: The Swift-Mountain-Dwelling Deity weds the Deity Princess-of-Great-Food and fathers eight deities, from the Deity Young-Mountain-Integrator to the Deity Lord-Stem-Tree-Young-House-Rope.

l: The August Deliberation for Pacifying the Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a deliberation The August Deliberation for Pacifying the Land concerns the divine consultation over how to subdue the violent and savage Earthly Deities and establish governance of the land.

l: Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: August child charged to govern the land, observes uproar from Heaven’s bridge, then re-ascends to report it.

l: Earthly Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Earthly Deities are numerous, violent, and savage; the divine assembly seeks a deity to subdue them.

l: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi is selected to subdue the Earthly Deities and sent to the Central Land of Reed-Plains; he immediately curries favour with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and brings no report for three years.

l: Heavenly-Young-Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Heavenly-Young-Prince, son of Deity Heaven's-Earth-Spirit, is sent to Reed-Plains to pacify savage Deities. Armed with heavenly bow and arrows, he marries Princess Under-Shining, fails to report for eight years, shoots Name-Crying-Female, and is killed by the returning arrow while asleep.

l: Deity Heaven's-Earth-Spirit, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_father_of Heavenly-Young-Prince Deity Heaven's-Earth-Spirit is the father of the Heavenly-Young-Prince. He comes down from Heaven with his wife and children after hearing the prince's wife's wailing and takes part in the mourning rites.

l: pheasant the Name-Crying-Female, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A female messenger pheasant is sent to question the Heavenly-Young-Prince’s delay, but is shot and killed after the Heavenly-Spying-Woman condemns its cry.

l: arrow, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Arrow bestowed on Heavenly-Young-Prince kills Name-Crying-Female, returns through its hole, then strikes and kills Heavenly-Young-Prince.

l: High-Integrating-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: High-Integrating-Deity, also called High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, sits with the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, finds blood on an arrow, sends it back to kill the Heavenly-Young-Prince, charges an august child with dominion, and commands Heaven's-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty to descend.

l: mourning-house, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A mourning-house at Mount Mourning is built for the Heavenly-Young-Prince, then Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne angrily cuts it down and kicks away its pieces.

l: Great-Blade-Mower, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_another_name_for Divine-Keen-Sabre [the great sword used to cut down the mourning-house] Great-Blade-Mower is one name of the great sword used by the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne to cut down the mourning-house.

l: Divine-Keen-Sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_another_name_for Great-Blade-Mower [the great sword used to cut down the mourning-house] Divine-Keen-Sabre is another name for the great sword used by the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne to cut down the mourning-house.

l: Song, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A Rustic Style song, sung by Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne’s younger sister to reveal his august name, describes him traversing two august valleys.

l: Deity Heavenly-Bird-Boat, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: A deity attached to Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity, sent to Inasa, who helped summon Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master and seek the Central Land’s yield.

l: Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm, son of Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, carries a thousand-draught rock and challenges Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity. His hand is transformed and crushed; he flees, then obeys his father and Deity Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master by supporting surrender of the Central Land of Reed-Plains.

l: His Augustness Heaven's-Sun-Height-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: His Augustness Heaven's-Sun-Height-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty is an august child of the Heavenly Deities, commanded by Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and High-Integrating-Deity to govern Central Land of Reed-Plains and rule Luxuriant Reed-Plain-Land-of-Fresh-Rice-ears. He agrees, receives the mirror, Herb-Quelling-Great-Sword, and several deities, leaves the Heavenly Rock-Seat, and descends through the clouds onto Kuzhifuru. He seeks marriage with Divine-Princess-of-Ata, rejects Princess-Long-as-the-Rocks, and weds Princess-Blossoming-Brilliantly-Like-the-Flowers-of-the-Trees for one night. When she says she is pregnant, he doubts the child is his and calls it an Earthly Deity's child.

l: dominion of the Central Land of Reed-Plains, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods)
s: is_a dominion [charged to the august child of the Heavenly Deity] The dominion of the Central Land of Reed-Plains was the dominion that the Heavenly Deities charged the august child with governing.

s: is_a abdication The abdication of the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land occurred after his sons agreed to follow the commands of the august child of the Heavenly Deities. He yielded the Central Land of Reed-Plains while requesting that a great abode be established for him and that Deity Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master respectfully serve his children.
